scenario: AITA for not hosting thanksgiving like I planned to | For about 50 years, my mom hosted all of her children and grandchildren for thanksgiving and Christmas Eve. She’s now gotten too old and asked us kids to take over the tradition. There are 4 of us so we just rotate. We’ve each hosted one holiday so far. This thanksgiving is my turn. We have never spent thanksgiving or Christmas Eve with my wife’s family. We’ve just never been as close to them plus they live all over the country. Well this year her mom and aunts decided to go to the Macy’s thanksgiving day parade. At first it was just a sister’s trip but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet them up there. My wife really wants to go. She hasnt seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter wants to go because it’s a “once in a lifetime event” (which i agree with). And I want to go. As soon as we decided to go I called my older brother to see what we should do about thanksgiving because I can’t host this year. He said our oldest sister is going to be pissed and i have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I call her and she is mad. She says she’ll probably have to end up hosting even though she is up next for Christmas and I’m being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. “Mom wouldn’t abandon thanksgiving to go to nyc” and went on about how sad mom will be that I’m doing this. I offered to pay for them to rent a spot and have it catered but she said that takes away from the close knit family vibe. My brother said his wife might be up for it but he didn’t sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can’t do it because she’s renovating her house. I do feel bad for backing out of my turn but I tried to offer up solutions and I also offered to host the next holiday—which my oldest sister said no to because it’s her turn and she’s been planning for it all year. Next up is my brother so I said me and him could maybe just swap thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Am I in the wrong here?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm in the wrong here. Let me start by understanding the situation. My mom used to host Thanksgiving and Christmas Eve for all her kids and grandkids for about 50 years. Now she's too old, so we, the four kids, are supposed to take turns hosting. So far, each of us has hosted one holiday. This year, it's my turn to host Thanksgiving. But here's the thing: my wife's family is planning to go to the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade. At first, it was just her sisters, but then they decided to invite all their kids and grandkids to meet up there. My wife really wants to go because she hasn't seen some of her aunts and cousins in years. Our daughter also wants to go because it's a once-in-a-lifetime event, and I agree with her. Plus, I want to go too. So, as soon as we decided to go, I called my older brother to figure out what we should do about Thanksgiving since I can't host this year. He told me that our oldest sister is going to be really mad and that I have to tell her myself. He wished me luck. So I called her, and she was mad. She said she'll probably end up hosting even though it's her turn for Christmas, and I'm being inconsiderate of what our mom asked us to do. She also mentioned that Mom would be sad if I abandon Thanksgiving to go to New York. I offered to pay for them to rent a place and have it catered, but she said that takes away from the close-knit family vibe. My brother mentioned that his wife might be up for hosting, but he didn't sound too happy about asking her. My other sister can't host because she's renovating her house. I feel bad about backing out of my turn, but I tried to offer solutions and also offered to host the next holiday, which my oldest sister said no to because it's her turn and she's been planning it all year. Next up is my brother, so I suggested that maybe me and him could swap Thanksgivings if his wife is up for it. Now, the question is: Am I in the wrong here? Should I be hosting Thanksgiving this year, or is it okay to go to the parade with my wife's family? First, I need to consider the expectations set by our mom. She hosted for 50 years, and now we're supposed to take turns. It's my turn this year, so there's an expectation that I'll host. But I have a valid reason for wanting to go to the parade with my wife's family. It's a special event, and it's important for my wife and daughter to connect with their extended family. On the other hand, my oldest sister is upset because she feels like I'm being inconsiderate of our mom's wishes and that she'll have to host again, which isn't fair because it's her turn for Christmas. My brother is also not too happy about the idea of his wife hosting, and my other sister can't host because of renovations. I tried to offer solutions, like paying for a rental and catering, but that didn't work because it changes the family vibe. I also offered to host the next holiday, but my sister refused. I suggested swapping with my brother, but that depends on his wife's willingness. So, am I in the wrong? It seems like I'm trying to balance my family obligations with my wife's family's plans. But is it fair to my siblings who are already hosting their turns? Or is it acceptable to prioritize this special event? I think it's important to consider the feelings of all family members. My oldest sister is upset, and my brother isn't too happy either. My mom would be sad if I don't host. But my wife and daughter are excited about this once-in-a-lifetime event. Maybe I should have communicated better with my siblings earlier. If I had talked to them before deciding to go, maybe we could have found a solution together. But I did call my brother right away to discuss it, which shows that I'm trying to be responsible. I also offered to help financially, which shows that I'm not completely abandoning my responsibility. But my sister didn't like that idea because it changes the family dynamic. In the end, I feel like I'm trying to do the right thing by considering everyone's feelings and offering solutions, but it's a tough situation. I don't think I'm entirely in the wrong, but I could have handled the communication better from the start.
